claims.statement: Inverter downtime, paid diagnostics, parts obligations, and funded modernization are evidenced events, so a readiness dossier can be tested at warranty expiry, support withdrawal, failure, or a planned repowering decision; no willingness to buy this exact independent dossier is established.

Commercial PV owners and O&M budget owners demonstrably fund maintenance, diagnostics, parts, and modernization, but no price test, conversion rate, repeat purchase, or annual-refresh commitment exists for the redesigned offer.

The founder can own the authored workflow, schema, and software and can retain only contractually permitted non-identifying derived records; no evidence yet shows that a derived dataset improves replacement decisions or produces repeat revenue.

Replacement decisions require site-specific electrical, topology, firmware, transformer, certification, and local-requirement checks, so the deliverable must be qualified-engineer reviewed and cannot be represented as a model-label compatibility lookup.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Asset manager, facilities or energy manager, business owner, or contracted O&M service lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Remain vendor-neutral, give the owner a portable evidence pack and competitive options, separate engineering review from equipment resale, and measure decision time and avoided rework rather than asserting scarcity
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The founder-controlled operating company for directly contracted readiness and project-management accounts; referring installers keep their independent customer relationships
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Direct contracts with asset owners, supported by nonexclusive installer/O&M referrals and workflow-integration agreements; the family installer can supply a bounded consenting pilot cohort

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Installer/O&M referral share plus direct account outreach and proposal work; require each channel and cohort to recover its acquisition cost from paid work rather than forecast renewals
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Customer prepays the defined dossier and pays project milestones before supplier commitments; no speculative hardware, long-lived reserve stock, refurbishment exposure, or obsolescence write-down is carried
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unknown until paid dossiers measure labor, engineer review, channel share, revisions, support, insurance allocation, and conversion to executed projects; the offer must pass on hardware and installation rather than warehouse them
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Founder-operated analytical workflow with bounded engineer review and delegated installation; each dossier requires an auditable assumptions, compatibility, certification, and decision record
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Professional and product-adjacent liability cover, legal and data-rights terms, cybersecurity, software, accounting, current technical requirements, document retention, and contractor governance
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis to test: a prepaid fleet-onboarding or site-readiness fee, a separately scoped qualified-engineering fee, and an optional project-management fee on an executed repair or repowering project; no annual fee is counted before a paid refresh
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Site-data collection and cleaning, document normalization, qualified engineer review, supplier quotation work, travel where unavoidable, payment fees, customer support, and project-specific subcontractors

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: OEMs, distributors, installers, engineering firms, and O&M providers can bundle the same diagnosis, compatibility work, and replacement procurement into existing service contracts
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is a commissioned site/fleet readiness dossier or an authorized repair/repowering project; measurable loss is non-production, emergency engineering and sourcing cost, or a delayed modernization decision
commercial_mechanics.payer: Commercial PV asset owner or the O&M party holding an authorized maintenance or modernization budget
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Warranty or OEM support expiry, a recorded fault, an unacceptable current lead time, an insurer or O&M readiness requirement, or a planned repowering budget cycle
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: A separately purchased annual portfolio refresh, a material site/configuration change, a new equipment cohort, or a later repair/repowering project; recurring demand is not assumed

contrary_evidence: SolarEdge and SMA offer rapid replacement pathways for eligible equipment, limiting the redesigned service to gaps where the OEM route is unavailable, unsuitable, or economically inferior.
Ordinary owner, EPC, installer, and O&M contracts can internalize spare planning, diagnostics, and repowering, so incumbents can bundle the redesigned workflow.
Supplier selection may prioritize performance and cost over lead time, weakening a readiness-led sales message.
Current technical and certification requirements plus site-level electrical constraints prevent a generic compatibility lookup from replacing qualified engineering.
No paid dossier, data-rights agreement, channel agreement, repeat order, or demonstrated decision improvement exists.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Company ownership and IP assignment for all founder-authored workflow code and schemas, with a mandatory customer data-rights agreement granting indefinite ownership of specifically defined non-identifying derived records while excluding ownership of raw customer data
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: If a customer refuses derived-data rights, deliver a paid isolated dossier without retaining its records; if an installer, engineer, or supplier refuses, use another qualified provider or return a bounded no-recommendation result rather than claiming compatibility
critical_control_point.current_owner: The founder-controlled company owns authored code, schemas, and workflow under IP assignment; customers retain raw site records, and the company owns only derived records expressly permitted by each signed data-rights clause
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The founder-controlled operating company for directly contracted readiness and project-management accounts; referring installers keep their independent customer relationships
critical_control_point.duration: Indefinite for company-owned IP and for only those non-identifying derived records whose signed data-rights grant expressly survives service termination
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder can create and assign the analytical workflow and software to the operating company; the family renewable-installation relationship offers a lawful pilot introduction but conveys no customer data or rights without consent
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The founder controls authorship, IP assignment, schema, software, and whether to accept an account; each customer controls raw-data disclosure, and a qualified engineer controls approval of site-specific recommendations
critical_control_point.renewal: Core IP ownership does not renew; customer monitoring, new raw-data access, and service rights require the applicable paid contract or renewal
critical_control_point.subject: Founder-authored repowering-readiness workflow software, normalized asset schema, and contractually permitted non-identifying derived compatibility and outcome records

economics.acquisition_route: Prepaid readiness engagements sold directly to asset owners through a bounded family-installer pilot, then repeatable nonexclusive installer/O&M referrals and direct portfolio sales
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A 5 million PLN founder-net-worth path exists only if paid dossiers become a repeatable multi-region workflow license or high-margin portfolio service with retained customer contracts and useful derived outcomes; a local one-off consultancy is insufficient, and current evidence does not establish the required conversion, margin, repeat rate, or defensibility
economics.founder_time: No more than five hours per day alongside employment, focused on data normalization, decision workflow, and account acceptance; qualified engineering, installation, and field work are contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Paid readiness and project-management revenue less referral share, founder delivery time, data normalization, engineering review, travel, software, insurance allocation, rework, and support; hardware and installation are pass-through or customer-direct
economics.payback: No inventory is funded; require each prepaid dossier to cover its acquisition, analytical, engineer-review, compliance, and support cost within that engagement before expanding the cohort
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: fixed fleet onboarding and per-site readiness fees, qualified-engineering work passed through or separately itemized, and a milestone-based project-management fee for executed repair or repowering
economics.retention_or_repeat: Paid refreshes after configuration or regulatory changes, new portfolio sites, and later repair or repowering projects; neither renewal nor repeat purchase is evidenced

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Company-owned workflow software and legally retained non-identifying configuration, quote, decision, and outcome records may improve future triage and procurement, but that improvement and its revenue effect remain unproven
fingerprint.customer: Polish commercial PV owners and O&M budget owners responsible for post-warranty, discontinued, or operationally critical inverter fleets
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct owner contracts introduced through nonexclusive installer and O&M referrals or workflow integrations, starting with consenting customers reachable through the family renewable-installation relationship
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Fixed-fee site or fleet repowering-readiness dossier plus optional paid procurement and project coordination for the selected repair or current-model replacement; no inventory reservation
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The asset owner or O&M budget owner pays when commissioning a readiness review, responding to a failure, or authorizing a replacement project; any annual refresh must be separately validated
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An inverter approaches warranty or support expiry, fails, or enters a planned modernization cycle without a documented compliant repair-versus-repowering route

founder_fit: The core workflow uses data normalization, decision analysis, and AI-assisted document handling rather than speculative hardware purchasing
A consenting pilot can begin through the family renewable-installation relationship without treating that relationship as customer ownership or exclusive distribution
Qualified engineers and installers can own field approval and execution while the founder stays within a five-hour daily limit
Prepaid bounded dossiers preserve capital and make contribution economics measurable before expansion

redesign.economic_effect: Replaces up to 100,000 PLN of speculative, slow-turning reserve inventory and its testing, storage, refurbishment, warranty, disposal, and write-down exposure with a 20,000 PLN capped software, legal, insurance, and contractor-validation budget. Customer prepayment funds bounded analysis and engineering review, while hardware remains customer-direct or pass-through; the change improves cash conversion but does not establish demand, contribution margin, repeat revenue, or scalable defensibility.

risks: Owners may buy engineering or repowering directly from OEMs, installers, or incumbent O&M providers
Customer documents may be incomplete and site-specific validation may prevent reusable automation
The company may incur professional liability if a dossier is mistaken for engineering approval or a compliance guarantee
No evidence yet shows that customers will pay for readiness before failure or purchase annual refreshes
Derived records may remain too sparse, restricted, or heterogeneous to create a useful data advantage
A service-heavy local model may fit the founder operationally but fail to compound toward the stated wealth objective

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: fixed fee engineering readiness dossier with optional repowering procurement and project coordination
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: company owned workflow software normalized schema and contractually permitted non identifying derived outcome records
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: qualified engineering review and compliant current equipment from replaceable authorized channels

structure.control_point: company-owned readiness workflow IP and contractually permitted non-identifying derived decision records
structure.critical_dependency: customer-authorized site records, qualified engineering approval, current certification, and competitively available compliant equipment

thesis: Future operating state (2034): owners of aging distributed PV fleets have a documented, engineering-ready route from each legacy inverter configuration to a currently compliant repair or repowering decision before a failure becomes an open-ended sourcing emergency. The business sells customer-authorized readiness dossiers and manages competitive execution; it does not speculate on legacy inventory or promise pooled swap stock.
title: Legacy Inverter Repowering Readiness Desk
uncertainties: Reachable count of post-warranty or unsupported commercial sites with a budget owner and a costly unresolved replacement decision
Willingness to prepay for a readiness dossier before failure and willingness to buy a later refresh
Fully loaded labor, engineering-review, insurance, channel, rework, support, and acquisition cost per paid dossier
Whether customers will grant usable derived-data rights while preserving confidentiality and raw-data ownership
Whether normalized outcomes improve decision time or accuracy beyond OEM, installer, engineering, and O&M offerings
A legally safe boundary between analytical workflow, engineering approval, equipment supply, and installation responsibility
Repeatable access to qualified engineers and compliant current-model supply without one irreplaceable partner
Whether the product can standardize and license enough workflow to escape a low-multiple local consultancy model
